writeup.headline: Microsoft rates a Buy on strong quality, a net-cash balance sheet and firm trend, held back by valuation.
writeup.thesis: Microsoft scores 66, a Buy with medium confidence, only 2 points above the Hold line at 65. The case rests on a near-perfect balance sheet score of 99 (net cash, with cash covering debt 1.91 times) and quality at 86, with a 46.8% operating margin, a 20.2% FCF margin and diluted shares down 0.2% year on year. Growth scores 65, with revenue up 17.8% year on year, though growth slowed by 0.6 pp from the previous quarter. Trend is strong at 76: the shares are 1.8% below their 52-week high and 19.8 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Valuation is the drag at 26. In absolute terms the multiples are high, at 11.9x sales, 59.2x FCF and 25.3x EV/EBIT, with the FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history valuation is near the middle overall, although P/FCF is more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends.
key_risks: The score sits just 2 points above Hold, so a small slip in any factor could lower the rating.
Valuation is high in absolute terms, with the FCF yield 3.5 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield.
The AI capex early warning is AMBER at 6/18, and heavy spending is weighing on free cash flow.
Competition from Anthropic and low Copilot penetration of commercial seats could limit AI monetisation.
Ongoing exposure to OpenAI dependence, the UK CMA cloud-licensing probe and the UK class action.
what_would_change: A drop of 2 or more points in the composite, for example from weaker FY27 Q1 results on October 28 or a softer trend, would move the rating to Hold.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 14 more points, most plausibly from a better valuation score or faster revenue growth.
A worsening of the capex early warning from AMBER could lead to the rating being capped.
Free cash flow recovering relative to price would improve P/FCF and the valuation score.
